# test/fixtures

Committed byte-pinned artifacts read by the deploy-gating suite.

Fixtures live here so tests can read a **file** instead of the **network**. Anything
in this directory is a historical artifact: it is not source, it is not maintained,
and it is not to be edited to make a red suite green.

---

## `f10-middleware.baseline.js`

The differential baseline for `test/perch-frame-headers.test.mjs`.

| | |
|---|---|
| What it is | `donovan-legal-site/functions/_middleware.js` as of commit `f833826` |
| Why `f833826` | main's tip immediately **before** #59 (PR #85) merged — the last pre-frame-headers middleware that ever served production ("F-10") |
| Blob id | `146284f47271013fef2e12c52bbd614f36abe990` |
| Size | 12,721 bytes, 220 LF, zero CR |
| Pinned | `-text` in `.gitattributes` |
| Read by | `test/perch-frame-headers.test.mjs`, describe block 3 |

`test/perch-frame-headers.test.mjs` proves that with `PERCH_ROUTER=off` the
middleware's response headers are **byte-identical** to this baseline. It proves it
differentially — it imports this file as a module and drives it through the same
harness — rather than by comparing against a hand-written expected header block,
which would only prove that the copy in the test matches the code in the test.

### Why it is a file and not a git read (#152)

The test used to read the baseline through git: `git rev-parse f833826:<path>`, and
on a miss `git fetch --depth=1 --no-tags origin f833826`.

`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` checks out with a bare `actions/checkout@v4` —
depth 1, no `fetch-depth` — so `f833826` is **not** in the CI clone and that fetch ran
on **every** run, including every production deploy. The `test` job is `npm test`, and
the `production` job declares `needs: [test, guard]`. A network blip, a GitHub
outage, or a garbage-collected unreferenced SHA therefore reddened a production
deploy for a reason that had nothing to do with the site. The assertion correctly
refuses to skip when it cannot read the baseline, which is precisely what made that
fragility load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

### Why the integrity check is stronger now, not weaker

Nothing was loosened to remove the network. The test recomputes this file's **git
blob SHA-1** — `sha1("blob " + length + NUL + bytes)` — and asserts it equals
`BASELINE_BLOB`.

A git blob id is a *content address*. That check proves the bytes **are** the F-10
bytes regardless of the filename, the path, or who handed them over. The old
`git rev-parse <commit>:<path>` proved something weaker: that some commit still names
that blob, and then trusted git to return the matching content.

This file is not a *copy* of that blob — it **is** the same git object:

```console
$ git rev-parse :test/fixtures/f10-middleware.baseline.js
146284f47271013fef2e12c52bbd614f36abe990
```

### Why the file carries no header comment

It must stay byte-identical to the blob it is pinned to. A `// regenerated by…`
banner inside it would change its bytes and break the very check that makes it
trustworthy. That is why the procedure lives here, in the test file, and in
`docs/F10-BASELINE-FIXTURE.md` instead.

### Why `-text` in `.gitattributes`

The hash is over raw bytes, and this repo runs `core.autocrlf=true`. Without the pin,
a Windows checkout would rewrite all 220 LF to CRLF, change the byte length, fail the
blob check locally, and stay green in CI — which checks out LF on Linux. `-text`
means: never convert this file. Two other artifacts in the repo are pinned the same
way and for the same reason (`swup.umd.js`, `openapi.v4.json`).

### Regenerating it

**Read `docs/F10-BASELINE-FIXTURE.md` first.** A baseline change is a deliberate
decision recorded in an order's report, never a fix for a red suite: a differential
baseline that follows the code under test measures nothing, which is the exact defect
(#59) that pinning it was introduced to remove.
